1 Samuel 17:1: The foreigners gathered their camps for war and assembled at Soccoth in Judea. They camped between Soccoth and Azekah at Epher-mem.

1 Samuel 17:3: The foreigners stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other, with the ravine between them.
1 Samuel 17:4: A mighty man came out from the foreigners’ battle line, named Goliath, from Gath. His height was four cubits and a span.
1 Samuel 17:5: A helmet was on his head, and he wore a coat of chain armour. His armour’s weight was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron.
1 Samuel 17:6: Bronze greaves were on his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders.
1 Samuel 17:7: His spear’s shaft was like a weavers’ beam, and its iron head weighed six hundred shekels. The one carrying his weapons walked before him.
1 Samuel 17:8: He stood and shouted to Israel’s battle line, “Why have you come out to draw up for war opposite us? Am I not a foreigner, and are you not Saul’s Hebrews? Choose a man for yourselves and let him come down to me.
1 Samuel 17:9: If he can fight me and strike me down, we will become your slaves. But if I prevail and strike him down, you will become our slaves and serve us.”
1 Samuel 17:10: The foreigner said, “Behold, I have defied Israel’s battle line today, on this day. Give me a man, and let the two of us fight in single combat.”
